execution.progress: Paid one-unit rounds; job, input, unit outcomes and lot persist across pauses; resuming pays only the remaining units after revalidation; completion, an unsuitable unit, cancelling and death settle once. No unattended progress.

details.costs: Study: 2 rounds. Prepare: inputStackId is the exact item id of your own edible food stack, quantity the whole units to prepare (at most its whole units); one round and 0.5 energy per unit, so 7 units take 7 rounds and 3.5 energy. Every round is checked before any charge; prepare resumes your paused work (inputStackId and quantity may be omitted). Inspect (inputStackId of your own food) and inspect-progress (your latest preparation): one round, 0.2 energy, no food used. Cancel: one round, no energy. No vessel, water, fuel, tool or ground surface is used or given. Eating and giving use eat and give at their own costs.
details.effects: Each paid round separates one whole unit from the input, checks it by eye and brushes it by hand, held, never set on the ground. A usable unit joins one owned lot of the same food with unchanged quantity, origin, age, decay, nutrition and toxicity, recorded as raw, unheated, dry-brushed, safety unknown. Loose soil on food is not represented, so no debris is measured or removed and no cleanliness is claimed. A spoiled unit is reported unsuitable, stays unprepared and ends the work. Nothing is cooked, peeled, washed, made safe or kept fresher; food keeps ageing, and the planting trial treats prepared units as processed. The lot holds only completed units. Inspections record visible condition, treatment and your own eating record (not a safety test) as an unverified personal record. An unworked round, too little energy, or an input no longer yours with a whole unit pauses without charge. Cancel or death ends the work; completed units stay. No refund or reward; nobody is fed.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Heat exposure trial
value.function: Inspect what the world represents about heat exposure here, at a visible point or object, then measure your own body temperature while staying where you are for 1-3 rounds and compare your records; no shade, shelter or cooling is made or assumed.
value.costs: Study: 2 rounds, 0.2 energy each. inspect: 1 round, 0.2; targetId (visible object or item) or x, y (visible point within 5), or neither for a survey. sample: only where you stand, sampleRounds 1-3 (default 1), 0.2 per sampled round; needs 0.2 energy, health 20+ and body 7-34 (activity guards, not safety); baselineId names an earlier record. compare: 1 round, 0.2, uses no sample. inspect-progress: 1 round, 0.2. resume: at the trial position, as sample. cancel: 1 round, no energy. Refusals cost nothing; nothing is used or given; travel is navigate.
value.effects: inspect gives your body and air readings (measured) and, here and at candidates (the nearest visible spot of each other ground kind and each visible enclosure interior, or the named one), model-derived air, indoor, light, insulation and next-round body change from the world's own update. Ground kind, time, weather, enclosure interiors (air pulled toward 12, insulation slowing change) and installed shelter or fire rules change exposure; trees, plants and rocks change no air, light or wind, so no shade is reported. sample records body temperature at each round's start and the next (measured), the prediction and the same-round open-soil value (model-derived). Trial end and compare label evidence, represented heat input, observed trend and body direction (cooling only if body temperature fell). Another action, moving or low energy pauses free; guards stop; death ends. No reward, buff, shelter or cooling.

execution.progress: sample pays and records one round at a time with the same action up to sampleRounds; each after reading is taken at the next round start. resume continues a paused trial; inspect, compare, inspect-progress and cancel take one round.

value.name: Vocal music
value.function: Hum or sing a short quiet phrase with your own voice for 1-3 rounds; nearby people hear each voiced round.
value.costs: Study: 2 rounds at 0.2 energy each; each hums a short practice phrase heard nearby (silent in pain or distress). hum or sing: rounds 1-3 (default 1), 0.5 energy per voiced round, no material. phrase: 2-8 notes {pitch: -4..4 steps from the home note 0, beats: 1-4}, or improvise=true. sing may add text (at most 240 characters, as tell). Shared by study, hum and sing: at most 3 voiced rounds in any 10 rounds, and 2 unvoiced rounds after 3 voiced rounds in a row or in one bout; a start must fit every requested round. Checked at start and each round: alive; no pain (an injury in the last round) or distress (satiety 0, body temperature below 7 or above 34); at least 0.5 energy. A refused start or resume costs nothing. resume continues a paused bout after fresh checks; cancel takes one round and no energy; both use only mode.
value.effects: Each voiced round is one segment at your position: everyone else living within 5 units (tell's hearing radius), seen or not, gets a heard event and heard-list entry with your mode, phrase, words and segment. Silence, refusals and pauses are not heard. The sound ends with each segment; no object, item, mark or lasting sound is made. Another action, a refused round, too little energy, a limit, pain or distress pauses the bout without charge; voiced segments and their energy are never refunded. Death ends the bout and any study. improvise=true derives 4-6 notes from your id and the start round (FNV-1a and xorshift32; from 0, steps of -2..+2 within -3..+3, back to 0), never at random. No reward, mood change or practice milestone; listeners get only the heard entry, and no reaction is implied.

execution.progress: hum or sing voices one segment per round and continues with the same action until the requested rounds are voiced; resume continues a paused bout; cancel takes one round. Voiced segments persist across pauses.
